findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed several food items stored in grocery store sacks in several freezers and the walk-in cooler. Grocery store sacks are not approved food-grade storage packagings. PIC was notified and staff started the process of repackaging the items using an available roll of approved food-grade bags. Ensure that food is protected from contamination by always using food-grade packaging for storage.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the kitchen hand washing sink was blocked with a bottle of soap and plastic when the inspector arrived. CORRECTED: The staff removed from the sink during the inspection. Ensure that hand washing sinks are maintained accessible for employee use at all times.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed that there was not a probe-style thermometer in the establishment. The PIC was informed and will have one available on or by a Follow Up Re-Inspection in 10 days (24 April 2026). Ensure that a food measuring device is readily available for use in measuring food temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the following:
(1) a buildup of soil residues on the shelves of the walk-in cooler.
(2) underneath the prep tables on a shelf was a paint scraper with with sticky green liquid.
The PIC was notified, and made plans to clean these areas more frequently.
Ensure that non-food contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned frequently to prevent the accumulation of soil residues.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed that the mop was sitting in the water part of the mop bucket where it is unable to air dry. CORRECTED: The PIC was informed that the mop was not properly stored, and the PIC removed the mop from the mop bucket and hung it to dry. Ensure that after use mops are able to fully air dry in a place where they cannot soil walls, equipment, or supplies.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Observed wet wiping cloths sitting on prep counters within the kitchen. The PIC was notified and the cloths were moved into the sanitizer bucket during the inspection. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are always stored in sanitizing solutions between uses.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed dirty water inside the mop bucket stored in the closet. The PIC stated that they last mopped this morning. During the inspection the water was dumped down the mop sink. Ensure that dirty mop water is always dumped after use.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee wash their hands in the dump sink during the inspection. The employee was educated that hand washing must only occur in designated hand washing sinks. After the education the employee rinsed their hands for about five seconds without soap and turned off the faucet with their bare hands in the hand washing sink. The inspector stepped in again and demonstrated the proper technique with the employee. After the demonstration the employee used the proper procedure, including using soap, scrubbing hands for 10-15 seconds, and using a barrier to turn off the faucet. The PIC was reminded of the importance of the proper hand washing procedure to avoid re-contaminating clean hands. Ensure that employees always wash hands in designated hand washing sinks and utilize the proper hand washing procedure.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed the kitchen hand washing sink was blocked with the soap dispenser and dishes when the inspector arrived. The items were removed from the sink during the inspection. Ensure that hand washing sinks are maintained accessible for employee use at all times.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the sanitizer bucket and triple sink were testing at 0 ppm (Cl) during the inspection. After the PIC added bleach to both they were testing at 150 ppm (Cl). The PIC was reminded about the importance of testing saniztier concentrations on a regular basis and changing them frequently. Ensure that sanitizing solutions are always testing at the correct concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed various single-use articles (including, but not limited too, take out bags, to-go boxes, and containers) stored directly on the floor next to the cash register. The PIC was educated about storing single-use articles at least 6-inches above the ground to avoid contamination. Ensure that all single-use articles are stored correctly by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed there is bare wood screwed into the wall behind the front hand washing sink. The inspector educated that bare wood is not a smooth, durable, or easily cleanable surface. The bare wood must be sealed (ex. painted). Ensure that the bare wood is sealed to be durable, smooth, and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed the food handlers training of one of the employees is expired (the certificate expired in 2023). The only other employee at the facility is a CFPM. Ensure that all food handlers, other than those with CFPM certificates, obtain training in basic food handling principles. The employee must obtain their food handler certificate by the next routine inspection.  

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Utensils are observed to be stored on soiled trays on tray rack in the kitchen. Ensure utensils are stored on cleaned and sanitized surfaces. Operators re-washed the untensils and discarded the trays voluntarily. Corrected on site. No follow-up required. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following cans to be damaged along the upper/lower seams which potentially introduces contaminants and breaks the seal of the can: 

5 Cans of Oyster Sauce
1 Can of Pineapple Juice
1 Can of Tomato Ketchup

During each delivery, ensure that cans are being delivered intact and in good condition and that no seams have damage. Cans that have damage along upper and/or lower seams must be discarded. Operator discarded all cans required to be discarded at the time of inspection. Corrected on site. 

3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Date marking in the walk in cooler was inconsistent. The majority of items appeared to have appropriate date marking. However, several items including but not limited to mushrooms, chicken nuggets and cut broccoli were observed to not have date marking. Ensure that date marking is consistent throughout the facility. TCS foods must be date marked when not used within twenty-four hours. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
An in-use knife was stored between counter tops in the kitchen. In-use utensils should be stored only on cleaned and sanitized surfaces. The areas between equipment are not cleaned and sanitized regularly. The knife was removed from between the counter tops and stored appropriately during inspection. Corrected on site. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
The three-compartment sink in the facility was available but had one of the three compartments blocked with equipment. The other compartments were filled with wash and sanitize solutions. There was no compartment available for rinsing due to being blocked with equipment. Ensure that all three compartments of the sink are unblocked and that the process of wash, rinse and sanitize is being followed correctly. 

4-301.12: (A) Sink with 3-compartments shall be provided for EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS. (B) Sinks shall be capable of accommodating the immersion of the largest piece of EQUIPMENT or UTENSIL. A machine or alternative option can be used. Reference 4-301.12 Pf (C) Alternative manual WAREWASHING EQUIPMENT may be used for special cleaning C

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
A piece of sheet metal behind the fryers was observed to be peeling away from the wall to the extent that an open gap had formed between the wall and metal panels. Reattach the metal to the wall to ensure the surface is smooth, durable and easily cleanable. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: Items int he walk-in cooler were observed to be without a date mark due to their addition to the cooler today. A date marked was placed during the inspection on all new items from today. Ensure dates are applied immediately upon prep to ensure their integrity.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The caulking by the triple sink was observed to be in need of repair. This violation was corrected on site with the application of clean tape to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The caulking of the triple sink, prep sink, and hand sink was observed to be in a state of disrepair. Ensure the old caulking is removed and fresh caulking is applied to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: REPEAT #1: Observed handwashing sink to be blocked by package of paper towels. Ensure handwashing stations are always accessible and used for handwashing only. Reference 5-205.11.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed handsink to be without soap. Ensure soap is always present when in operation. Corrected. Soap was provided. Reference 6-301.11.
Observed plastic bin to be blocking sink upon arrival of inspection. Ensure sinks are always accessible. Corrected. Handwashing station was made accessible. Reference 5-205.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed clean equipment to be placed on trays that have residue. Clean equipment must be placed in location that is clean. Clean storage area. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: Observed several foods without date mark. This included noodles and chicken in the walk-in cooler. PIC stated all products had been made less than 7 days ago. Products will be datemarked with appropriate date. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed heavy residue on handsink handles. Clean handles to prevent build-up. Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.comment: Observed handsink in front area to have no water available. Ensure potable water with hot and cold water for handsink is available during all times of operation. Corrected. PIC turned water on. In addition, PIC stated during cleaning water is turned off. Reference 5-103.11 .

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment: Observed raw meat above RTE food. Ensure no raw meats are stored above RTE foods. Corrected. RTE food was relocated . Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: Observed several different products without date marks. This included egg rolls and chicken in W-I Cooler and egg rolls in (S) fridge. Corrected. PIC stated all foods are less than 7 days old. Education provided. All products will be labeled appropriately. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment: Observed several different bulk products to be unlabeled. All bulk items must be properly labeled. Label bulk items with common name. Reference 3-601.11.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Observed several foods to be uncovered. This includes egg rolls and chicken. Ensure all foods are covered. Corrected. Foods have been covered.  Reference 3-307.11.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: Observed wiping cloth to be setting next to rice cooker on prep table. Ensure all wiping cloths are placed in appropriate areas. Corrected. Wiping cloth was placed in designated area. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Observed black residue in bathroom ceiling. Ensure physical facilities are cleaned as needed to prevent accumulation. Clean bathroom. Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: Arrived to facility with no CFM present. CFM arrived at facility shortly after. Ensure CFM is always present during hours of preparation.
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed several knives to be soiled with debris laying in "designated" clean area. Ensure all equipment and utensils are cleaned properly and placed in clean areas. Corrected. PIC will clean equipment.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) food contact surface is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed food handler license expired. Ensure all food employees have food handler's license. Obtain certificate. 
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed several items to be out of temperature including: Pork (probed at 45F), Egg rolls (probed at 46F), and Beef (probed at 46F). PIC stated cooler is left open during lunch period 11:00-12:00. Furthermore, PIC stated food is used up everyday. During this lunch period, chicken was placed next to stove (probed at 46F). Ensure food is maintained at 41F or below. Close cold holding unit when not in use. Do not remove food from cooling unit when not in use. Corrective Action. Food was placed in cooling unit and the unit was closed to lower temperature. 
750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Cooling unit has not cooled products since lunch items were placed in cooler. Internal temperature of unit is >50F. Time and Temperature for Control and Safety (TCS) foods cannot be stored in unit. Corrective action. All TCS foods are placed in another cooling unit. PIC attempted to change the temperature of the unit prior to cooling lunch foods. Fix unit before using to store TCS foods. 
750-140 All refrigeration units used to store potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F or below.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed chicken in both chest freezers to be unprotected. Ensure food is covered and protected during storage. 
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed several boxes of chicken to be on floor of walk-in cooler sitting on metal trays. Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off of floor. Place food at least 6 inches off the floor. 
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed handle of tongs to be touching food in cold holding unit. Ensure dispensing utensils are properly placed to prevent potential cross-contamination. 750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
findings.comment:
Observed right faucet of 3-compartment sink to be unoperational. PIC turned on faucet. Faucet had potable cold and hot water. No leaks were observed. PIC stated faucet is turned off over weekend. Ensure equipment is in good repair. 
750-820 For manual washing, rinsing and sanitizing utensils and equipment, each compartment of the sink shall be supplied with hot and cold potable running water.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed multiple bulk items to be without label. All bulk items removed from original packaging must have label on container. Label containers with common name of product.
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.comment:
Observed eggs and uncut onions below beef in walk-in cooler. Properly store all foods in order of cooking temperature. Onions must be stored above eggs. Eggs must be stored above beef. Rearrange food for proper storing techniques. 
750-130(d)  All raw meat shall be properly stored, store in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed bottom of pan to be sitting on broccoli. Ensure food is protected from cross-contamination. Remove pan to prevent food-contact
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed water to be leaking from walk-in cooler pipeline. Fix leak to prevent cross-contamination. 
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed clean utensils to be soiled with debris and placed on unclean surface. Ensure all food equipment is properly cleaned. Clean utensils.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment:
Observed soap bottle and sponge sitting in handwashing station. Ensure handwashing stations are accessible at all times. Remove items. 
750-1120(b) Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed no soap available for handwashing stations. Soap must be available at all times. Retrieve necessary supplies. 
750-1120e A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed bulk powders throughout the kitchen to not be labeled with the common name of the item. Label all items removed from their original packaging.
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
1) Observed raw beef stored above peppers, and raw chicken wings stored above raw shrimp in the walk in cooler. Store foods in order of cooking temperature with the highest final cooking temperature on the bottom. 2) Observed personal foods intermingled with food for the public in the chest freezer (eel) and in the walk in cooler (vegetables). Personal foods shall be stored in a designated area below and away from food for the public to avoid the risk of potential contamination.
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed egg rolls in the walk in cooler underneath the fan unit to not be covered. Cover all foods to protect from contamination, especially since this is right next to a drip from the fan unit that is being collected into a basin.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed cups being used as scoops in bulk powders and granules. Use scoops with handles and store with the handle extended up and out of the food.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed a wet wiping cloth sitting on the chest freezer in the back. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution in between use.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed leaks at the prep sink and the front hand sink near the register. Repair faucets so that they do not leak when off.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: 750-530(a) Observed personal food and drinks stored in prep areas and intermingled with food for service to the general public. Personal food and drinks shall be stored in designated areas away from food for the general public or from food contact surfaces of clean, sanitized dishware or food equipment to prevent potential contamination.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-650(a) Observed eggs rolls stored on top of paper towels in storage to soak oil. Food contact surfaces must be smooth, non-absorbant and easily cleanable. Cease to use paper towels to soak grease from egg rolls. Paper was removed to correct the violation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800(e) Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the outer rims of the rice cookers with food debris; 2) the sides of the cook line with an accumulation of grease; and 3) the exterior of the coolers and large equipment with food splash and grease accumulation.
